question.text: For the elementary reaction <math><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, the rate of disappearance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> increases by a factor of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn></math> upon doubling the concentration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math>. The order of the reaction with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> is

solution.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mfenced open="[" close="]" separators="|"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></msup><msup><mfenced open="[" close="]" separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></msup></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>
